title: 🗺️ UNIT 8: GEOGRAPHICAL ENQUIRY AND MAP MAKING
notes: Geographical enquiry :- systematic investigation of geographic phenomena using research skills, data, maps and modern technologies.

title: 🔬 8.1 FUNDAMENTALS OF RESEARCH IN GEOGRAPHY
notes:
Research → a systematic and objective search for reliable knowledge or solutions to identified problems.

It involves:
🔹 Inquiry for dependable information.
🔹 Scientific study of a problem.
🔹 Systematic collection and analysis of evidence.
🔹 Objective search for knowledge.

⭐ Geographic research focuses especially on relationships between people, places, space and the environment.

title: 🎯 8.1.1 PURPOSE OF UNDERTAKING RESEARCH
notes:
Research helps investigate problems, develop knowledge and support decision-making.

Five major purposes →

1️⃣ Exploration → investigate poorly understood phenomena and identify important variables.

2️⃣ Description → document and characterize a phenomenon.

3️⃣ Explanation → determine why a phenomenon occurs or has a particular pattern.

4️⃣ Understanding → examine processes and interactions between people and phenomena.

5️⃣ Prediction → forecast possible future outcomes and behaviors.

⭐ Explore → Describe → Explain → Understand → Predict.

title: 🌍 8.1.2 FEATURES OF GEOGRAPHIC RESEARCH
notes:
Geographic research commonly focuses on:

🔹 Location and spatial distribution.
🔹 Spatial patterns and relationships.
🔹 Interaction between people and environment.
🔹 Physical and human processes.
🔹 Causes of geographic patterns.
🔹 Changes through time.

⭐ Geography links physical sciences, social sciences and humanities through the study of space, place and environment.

title: 🧩 8.1.3 RESEARCH APPROACH & METHODOLOGY
notes:
A research project has three broad components:

🔹 Subject matter → what is being studied?

🔹 Methodology/Approach → how is it studied?

🔹 Philosophical basis → assumptions about reality and knowledge.

Research approach → overall direction or strategy of investigation.

Methodology → framework explaining how research is designed and carried out.

Method → specific technique used to collect or analyze data.

title: 📊 8.1.4 QUALITATIVE & QUANTITATIVE APPROACHES
notes:
🔵 Quantitative approach → uses numerical data, measurement and statistical analysis.

Examples → questionnaires with numerical responses + measurements + statistical datasets.

🟢 Qualitative approach → investigates meanings, experiences, perceptions and processes using non-numerical information.

Examples → interviews + observations + discussions + documents.

⭐ Quantitative = numbers and measurement.
⭐ Qualitative = meanings, experiences and descriptions.

title: 🔄 8.1.5 MIXED-METHOD RESEARCH
notes:
Mixed-method research → combines qualitative and quantitative approaches in one study.

🔹 Quantitative data → measures patterns and relationships.

🔹 Qualitative data → explains experiences, meanings and reasons.

⭐ Combining both approaches can provide a broader understanding of a geographic problem.

title: 📝 8.1.6 BASIC ELEMENTS OF RESEARCH
notes:
A geographic research project generally involves:

1️⃣ Identify the problem.
2️⃣ Review relevant information.
3️⃣ Formulate research questions or objectives.
4️⃣ Select an appropriate approach and methods.
5️⃣ Collect data.
6️⃣ Organize and analyze data.
7️⃣ Interpret the findings.
8️⃣ Draw conclusions.
9️⃣ Make recommendations.
🔟 Communicate the results.

⭐ Good research follows a planned, logical and systematic process.

title: 💡 8.1.7 RESEARCH PROBLEM & QUESTIONS
notes:
Research problem → a clearly identified issue or question requiring investigation.

Good research questions should be:
🔹 Clear
🔹 Focused
🔹 Researchable
🔹 Relevant to the problem
🔹 Answerable using available evidence

⭐ A well-defined problem guides the entire research process.

title: 📚 8.1.8 LITERATURE REVIEW
notes:
Literature review → examination of existing information and research related to the topic.

Purposes →
🔹 Understand what is already known.
🔹 Identify gaps in knowledge.
🔹 Develop the research framework.
🔹 Avoid unnecessary duplication.
🔹 Provide background for interpreting results.

Sources may include → books + journals + reports + maps + databases + previous research.

title: 📥 8.1.9 DATA COLLECTION
notes:
Data → information collected for research and analysis.

🔵 Primary data → collected directly by the researcher.
Examples → field measurements + observations + interviews + questionnaires + surveys.

🟢 Secondary data → previously collected by other people or institutions.
Examples → reports + maps + census data + published research + existing databases.

⭐ Primary = first-hand.
⭐ Secondary = already available.

title: 📋 8.1.10 DATA COLLECTION METHODS
notes:
Common methods include:

👀 Observation → systematic recording of phenomena.

🗣️ Interview → obtaining information through direct questioning.

📝 Questionnaire → structured questions answered by respondents.

🌍 Field survey → collecting information directly from the study area.

📏 Measurement → obtaining numerical values using appropriate instruments.

📚 Document analysis → extracting information from existing records and sources.

⭐ The method should match the research question and type of information required.

title: 📊 8.1.11 DATA ANALYSIS & INTERPRETATION
notes:
Data analysis → organizing and examining collected information to identify patterns, relationships and meanings.

Quantitative analysis may use →
🔹 Tables
🔹 Percentages
🔹 Graphs
🔹 Statistical measures

Qualitative analysis may involve →
🔹 Categorizing information.
🔹 Identifying themes.
🔹 Comparing explanations.
🔹 Interpreting meanings.

⭐ Analysis transforms collected data into useful evidence.

title: 📄 8.1.12 RESEARCH REPORT
notes:
A research report communicates the investigation and its findings.

Important components →
🔹 Title
🔹 Introduction/background
🔹 Research problem and objectives
🔹 Methodology
🔹 Results/findings
🔹 Discussion
🔹 Conclusion
🔹 Recommendations
🔹 References

⭐ Conclusion → answers the research problem using the findings.
⭐ Recommendations → propose actions or further research.

title: 🗺️ 8.2 GIS DATA & MAP MAKING USING GIS
notes:
GIS → Geographic Information System; a technology for capturing, storing, manipulating, analyzing, managing and presenting geographic information.

⭐ GIS data is mainly spatial → information is linked to a particular location.

GIS can be used to:
🔹 Create digital maps.
🔹 Store geographic information.
🔹 Analyze spatial relationships.
🔹 Display patterns.
🔹 Support planning and decision-making.

title: 🧩 8.2.1 FIVE COMPONENTS OF GIS
notes:
GIS has five fundamental components:

1️⃣ Data → geographic information used for analysis.
2️⃣ Hardware → computers and other physical equipment.
3️⃣ Software → programs used to manage and analyze geographic data.
4️⃣ People → users who operate and apply GIS.
5️⃣ Methods → procedures and techniques used to collect, analyze and present information.

⭐ GIS = Data + Hardware + Software + People + Methods.

title: 📍 8.2.2 GIS DATA
notes:
GIS data is geographic information that can be mapped and analyzed.

Two major sources →
🔵 Primary data → obtained directly from the ground or field.

Examples → field surveys + GPS measurements + remote sensing imagery.

🟢 Secondary data → obtained from existing sources.

Examples → paper maps + existing digital datasets + institutional records.

⭐ GIS connects information with geographic location.

title: 🔷 8.2.3 VECTOR DATA
notes:
Vector data represents geographic features using geometric objects:

📍 Point → represents a specific location.
Example → school, well or hospital.

📏 Line → represents linear features.
Example → road, river or railway.

⬛ Polygon → represents areas.
Example → district, lake or land-use zone.

⭐ Vector → Point + Line + Polygon.

title: 🟩 8.2.4 RASTER DATA
notes:
Raster data represents geographic information using a grid of cells or pixels.

Each cell contains a value representing information about that location.

Common uses →
🔹 Satellite imagery
🔹 Elevation data
🔹 Temperature surfaces
🔹 Rainfall distribution
🔹 Land-cover information

⭐ Raster = grid of cells.
⭐ Vector = points, lines and polygons.

title: 🏷️ 8.2.5 ATTRIBUTE DATA
notes:
Attribute data → descriptive information associated with geographic features.

Example → a school point may have attributes such as:
🔹 Name
🔹 Number of students
🔹 Type of school
🔹 Location

⭐ Spatial data tells WHERE; attribute data tells WHAT.

title: 📥 8.2.6 GATHERING DATA FOR GIS
notes:
GIS data can be gathered from:

🔹 Field surveys.
🔹 GPS measurements.
🔹 Remote sensing imagery.
🔹 Existing maps.
🔹 Census and statistical data.
🔹 Government and institutional datasets.
🔹 Existing digital geographic databases.

⭐ Data quality, accuracy and appropriate geographic reference are essential for reliable GIS analysis.

title: 🛰️ 8.2.7 REMOTE SENSING
notes:
Remote sensing → obtaining information about Earth's surface without direct physical contact, commonly using sensors carried by satellites or aircraft.

Uses →
🔹 Land-use mapping.
🔹 Vegetation monitoring.
🔹 Weather and environmental observation.
🔹 Resource assessment.
🔹 Disaster monitoring.

⭐ Remote sensing provides valuable spatial data for GIS.

title: 📐 8.2.8 MAP MAKING USING GIS
notes:
GIS supports the production of different maps, including:

🗺️ Administrative maps → boundaries and administrative units.

⛰️ Topographic maps → terrain and physical features.

💧 Watershed maps → drainage and catchment areas.

Basic process →
Data collection → Data input → Data organization → Spatial analysis → Map design → Map presentation.

title: 🔍 8.2.9 GIS DATA ANALYSIS
notes:
GIS analysis examines spatial patterns, relationships and interactions.

Important techniques include:
🔹 Query → retrieve information matching selected conditions.

🔹 Buffering → creates zones around geographic features.

🔹 Overlay → combines layers to examine relationships.

🔹 Network analysis → analyzes connected linear features and movement.

🔹 Spatial analysis → investigates geographic patterns and relationships.

⭐ GIS turns geographic data into information useful for decision-making.

title: 🔗 8.2.10 VECTOR OVERLAY
notes:
Vector overlay → combines vector layers to identify relationships between geographic features.

Three important functions →

🔹 Clip → extracts features within a specified boundary.

🔹 Intersect → identifies areas where input layers overlap.

🔹 Union → combines polygon layers and retains features from both layers.

⭐ Overlay = combining spatial layers to obtain new information.

title: 🟩 8.2.11 RASTER OVERLAY
notes:
Raster overlay → combines raster layers by comparing corresponding cells.

When raster layers have the same resolution and aligned pixels, corresponding cell values can be combined to create a new raster layer.

Main approaches →
🔹 Spatial analysis tools.
🔹 Overlay operations.
🔹 Map algebra.

⭐ Raster overlay analyzes relationships between cell values across layers.

title: 🚗 8.2.12 NETWORK ANALYSIS
notes:
Network → a set of interconnected linear features through which movement or resources can flow.

Examples → roads + railways + streets + canals + rivers + transport routes.

Network analysis can be used for:
🔹 Pathfinding → finding the shortest or least-cost route.
🔹 Allocation → assigning network areas to facilities or services.
🔹 Tracing → identifying connected portions of a network.
🔹 Spatial interaction → analyzing accessibility and movement between locations.
🔹 Distance matrix → calculating distances between location pairs.
🔹 Location-allocation → locating facilities and allocating demand.

title: 📊 8.2.13 STATISTICAL DIAGRAMS & GIS
notes:
GIS can help construct and present statistical information geographically.

Common visual forms →
🔹 Bar diagrams
🔹 Pie diagrams
🔹 Line graphs
🔹 Thematic maps

⭐ Combining statistics with location helps reveal spatial patterns and differences.

title: 🧠 UNIT 8 KEY DIFFERENCES
notes:
🔬 Research → systematic search for reliable knowledge.

🎯 Exploration → investigates poorly understood phenomena.

📝 Description → documents characteristics.

❓ Explanation → identifies causes.

🧩 Understanding → examines processes and interactions.

🔮 Prediction → forecasts future outcomes.

🔵 Quantitative → numerical data.

🟢 Qualitative → meanings and experiences.

🔄 Mixed methods → combines both.

📥 Primary data → collected directly.

📚 Secondary data → obtained from existing sources.

📍 Vector → points + lines + polygons.

🟩 Raster → grid cells/pixels.

🏷️ Attribute → descriptive information linked to geographic features.

🗺️ GIS → captures + stores + manages + analyzes + presents geographic data.

🧩 GIS components → Data + Hardware + Software + People + Methods.

🔗 Vector overlay → Clip + Intersect + Union.

🚗 Network analysis → pathfinding + allocation + tracing + spatial interaction + distance matrix + location-allocation.
